description: The NGS antenna calibration site provides GNSS antenna calibrations for specific antenna types, identified by antenna code and radome code, which NGS uses in processing GNSS data for all its products and services. Contents: complete downloadable files of absolute antenna calibrations in ANTEX and ANTINFO formats, antenna metadata pages by company brand and model with photographs, diagrams, height measurement points and written descriptions, and per-antenna downloads of absolute calibrations in the IGS20 frame; older products such as IGS08 calibrations are available on request. The page notes that IGS20 replaced IGS14 on 2 October 2022, that NGS offers composite calibration files in both frames during a transition, and that mixing frames may cause several centimetres of positioning error. NGS also calibrates survey-grade antennas from qualified providers. Producer: NOAA National Geodetic Survey, United States; the calibrations apply worldwide. Coverage: global antenna models. Access: public downloads and web pages. Licence and cost: free; no licence text read. Caveats: calibration values must match the reference frame of the orbits and station coordinates used. Simulation uses: correct antenna models are needed in precise positioning and timing analyses of GNSS-dependent infrastructure. Related record: IGS precise products (data-igs-gnss-products), which use the same calibration conventions.
